question.text: For independent valuation of investments under the scheme of the Vindhya Event-Driven Fund (Cat III), the AIF Manager must appoint an independent valuer with:

answer.text: A minimum of 3 years of experience in valuation of unlisted securities.
A minimum of 1 year of experience in valuation of unlisted securities.
A minimum of 5 years of experience in valuation of listed securities only.
A CFA qualification only, regardless of experience.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Under the AIF framework, the independent valuer must have a minimum of 3 YEARS of experience in valuation of UNLISTED securities. This experience threshold ensures the valuer can appropriately mark private/illiquid positions — especially relevant for Cat III funds that hold side-pocketed illiquid tranches or event-driven stakes. APMI empanelment additionally standardises valuer quality. **The Trap:** Option B understates the experience floor. Option C confuses listed vs unlisted focus. Option D invents a qualification-only rule. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C, XIX-D test the 3-year unlisted rule identically. XXI-B (PM) has a different valuer regime. XV (RA) tests valuation methodologies, not valuer appointment. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** For a Cat III event-driven fund with side-pocket carve-outs, pick a valuer empanelled with APMI who has merger-arb and CDS-linked valuation experience. Quarterly IC reviews should include valuer methodology disclosures — document any reliance on Level-3 inputs in the PPM audit file.
